method: Opened original fig-220.png first, derived its complete inventory, then opened original fig-221.png and derived its inventory. These observations were committed to this file before reading downstream evidence. Approximate screen locations are identification aids, not measured physics.

inventory.fact: One panel with a single coordinate frame K1. X1 points right, Y1 up, Z1 obliquely down-left, meeting at O1 below the rear of the spacecraft. K1 is printed by the vertical frame axis. No unprimed ground frame is visible.

A horizontal right-facing spacecraft silhouette with a pointed nose, upper and lower body lines and two rear fins. The body is above, not coincident with, the horizontal X1 axis. The rear is near the vertical Y1 line. Hull contours and fin angles are not measured givens.

Two circular clock-like devices with dial marks and hands inside the body: rear-left B and forward-right A. A is to the right of B. Letter labels are separate from their clock faces. There are no printed clock times or numbered dial readings.

A starburst-like light source between the two clocks, approximately horizontally centered between them at their height. C is a separate tick and label on the X1 axis vertically below the light source, not printed on the light source itself. O1 is left of B and is not the emission position.

Wavy paths extend from near the central starburst toward both clocks, left toward B and right toward A. The source wave strokes have no independently legible arrowheads. Wave count, amplitude and the drawn gaps at endpoints are not numerical givens.
No second panel, velocity label, time label, units, numerical distance, origin-at-emitter claim or historical emblem is visible. Source labels use subscript-like 1, not apostrophes.

relationships: O1 lies left of B, light source and A.
B, central light source and A share approximately one horizontal line.
Light source is above the marked axis position C.
B and A are on opposite sides of the central source, approximately equally spaced in this schematic.
Both wavy paths belong to this one spacecraft/frame.

inventory.fact: Exactly two side-by-side panels, left labelled Cyrillic a and right Cyrillic b. Both depict the same right-facing spacecraft experiment with two clocks and a central emitter. They are different events, not two unrelated coordinate sketches.

Left panel has coincident K and K1 frames: paired labels Y,Y1 on one up axis, X,X1 on one right axis, Z,Z1 on one oblique down-left axis. O and O1 mark coincident origins at the rear, below the spacecraft. K and K1 labels are both visible beside the vertical axis.

Left spacecraft silhouette is above the shared X axis, rear near the shared Y axis and nose to the right. Rear fins and body/nose remain schematic. A starburst is inside approximately midway between the left and right clocks.

Left panel shows a rear-left clock face and a forward-right clock face labelled A. A separate B letter is not clearly visible beside the left clock in this source crop. C is a tick on the shared horizontal axis directly below the starburst. O/O1 is not C and is not the starburst.
Left panel has a starburst with short radial strokes but no traversing wavy paths. Both clock faces have visible marks/hands without printed time values.

Right panel separates the ground origin O and spacecraft origin O1 horizontally: O is left, O1 is right. Two distinct up axes Y and Y1 and two distinct down-left axes Z and Z1 share one horizontal X/X1 direction line. K is beside the ground Y axis, K1 beside the moving Y1 axis. X and X1 are labelled near separate right-pointing axis tips.

A velocity indication v with a right-pointing vector mark is above the rear of the spacecraft, accompanied by a horizontal right-pointing arrow. Motion direction is positive X; no numerical speed is printed.

Right spacecraft is shifted right relative to ground O. Its rear remains near the moving Y1 axis. B is the rear-left clock and A the forward-right clock. The starburst is between them; C remains a separate axis tick vertically below the starburst. O1 remains left of B, not at the starburst.

Wavy light paths run left and right from near the starburst. The left path reaches the B-clock vicinity; the right path stops substantially before the A-clock vicinity. This asymmetry is clearly visible. No independently legible arrowheads or printed numeric path lengths occur.
Both circular clock faces have dial marks and hands. The source contains no printed numerical reading; precise hand-angle physics cannot be inferred from these small historical marks.

No numerical time, distance, speed, ruler/grid, historical emblem or origin-at-emitter claim is visible. Subscript-like 1 denotes the moving frame. Panel letters and ink/texture are edition-normalizable, not mathematical givens.

relationships: Panel a: K and K1 origins/axes coincide.
Panel b: O1 is strictly to the right of O, with both frames parallel and positive X directed right.
In each panel: B-clock, source and A-clock are collinear in the spacecraft, with source approximately centered.
